messages.subject: Naive question about random year effects and initial values (Multivent model)
parts:
Hi everyone!

I have a very specific doubt about how to specify correctly random year effects and their initial values on a multievent capture-recapture model.

Some context: I am studying differences in survival between breeders and floaters individuals in a wild population of birds. I have fitted a model with additive effects of time and sex for survival (phi) and transition (psi) probabilities, and with recapture probability (p) only varying with sex.

I wanted to add a yearly random effect for both phi and psi probabilities. So I did it this way (I'll show a very simplified chunk of code, without the loops and matrices, because I only have  doubts about how to correctly specify random effects, everything works perfectly in the code I have)

# Phi
    logit(phiT[i,t]) <- betaT[sex[i]] + time_phiT[t] # logit for the survival of T(erritorials)
    logit(phiF[i,t]) <- betaF[sex[i]] + time_phiF[t] # logit for the survival of F(floaters)

# Psi
    logit(psiT[i,t]) <- etaT[sex[i]] + time_psiT[t] #logit for the transition of T(erritorials)
    logit(psiF[i,t]) <- etaF[sex[i]] + time_psiF[t] #logit for the transition of T(erritorials)

# Priors for survival
   # Phi
 betaT[1] ~ dnorm(0, 1.5) # for males
 betaT[2] ~ dnorm(0, 1.5) # for females
 betaF[1] ~ dnorm(0, 1.5) # for males
 betaF[2] ~ dnorm(0, 1.5) # for females

# Yearly random effect
lambda.sigmaT ~ dunif(0, 10)
   lambda.sigmaF ~ dunif(0, 10)  
   for(t in 1:(T-1)){
     time_phiT[t] ~ dnorm(0, sd = lambda.sigmaT)
     time_phiF[t] ~ dnorm(0, sd = lambda.sigmaF)
   }
 

 # Priors for transition
  # Psi
 etaT[1] ~ dnorm(0, 1.5) # for territorial males
 etaT[2] ~ dnorm(0, 1.5) # for  territorial females
 etaF[1] ~ dnorm(0, 1.5) # for floater males
 etaF[2] ~ dnorm(0, 1.5) # for floater females
 
 lambda.sigma2T ~ dunif(0, 10)  
  lambda.sigma2F ~ dunif(0, 10)  
    for(t in 1:(T-1)){
     time_psiT[t] ~ dnorm(0, sd = lambda.sigma2T)
     time_psiF[t] ~ dnorm(0, sd = lambda.sigma2F)
   }


   for(t in 1:(T-1)){
      phi_maleT[t] <- ilogit(betaT[1] + time_phiT[t])
      phi_femaleT[t] <- ilogit(betaT[2] + time_phiT[t])
      phi_maleF[t] <- ilogit(betaF[1] + time_phiF[t])
      phi_femaleF[t] <- ilogit(betaF[2] + time_phiF[t])
}



  for(t in 1:(T-1)){
   psi_maleT[t] <- ilogit(etaT[1] + time_psiT[t])
   psi_femaleT[t] <- ilogit(etaT[2] + time_psiT[t])
   psi_maleF[t] <- ilogit(etaF[1] + time_psiF[t])
   psi_femaleF[t] <- ilogit(etaF[2] + time_psiF[t])
 }

initial.values <- list(
                                  betaT = rnorm(2, 0, 1),
                                  betaF = rnorm(2, 0, 1),
                                  etaT = rnorm(2, 0, 1), 
                                  etaF = rnorm(2, 0, 1),
                                  lambda.sigmaT = runif(1, 0, 3),
                                  lambda.sigmaF = runif(1, 0, 3),
                                  lambda.sigma2T = runif(1, 0, 3),
                                  lambda.sigma2F = runif(1, 0, 3),
                                  z = zinit)

____________________________________________________________________________________

My main concern is that in the initial values part I don't provide any initial value for time_phiT, time_phiF, time_psiT and time_psiF and I get the following warning from NIMBLE when I run the model:

NAs were detected in model variables: time_phiT, logProb_time_phiT, time_phiF, logProb_time_phiF, time_psiT, logProb_time_psiT, time_psiF, logProb_time_psiF, phiT, phi_maleT, phi_femaleT, phiF, phi_maleF, phi_femaleF, psiT, psi_maleT,  [and more terms]

I guess this warning appears because I am not providing initial values for that part of the models but if I am understanding everything properly, these terms are dependent on lambda.sigmaT etc so I don't have to provide additional initial values for them, am I right? However I am little concerned about the NA warning for the phi and psi parameters, does it affect my estimates? Because when I call MCMCsummary for those parameters I don't see any strange thing, everything is quite fine.

I am also confused because in some scripts I have found in this forum some people specify initial values for these terms and I don't know if it is right!

initial.values <- list(betaT = rnorm(2, 0, 1),
                                  betaF = rnorm(2, 0, 1),
                                  etaT = rnorm(2, 0, 1), 
                                  etaF = rnorm(2, 0, 1),
                                  lambda.sigmaT = runif(1, 0, 3),
                                  lambda.sigmaF = runif(1, 0, 3),
                                  lambda.sigma2T = runif(1, 0, 3),
                                  lambda.sigma2F = runif(1, 0, 3),
                                  time_phiT = rep(0, my.constants$T-1),
                                  time_phiF = rep(0, my.constants$T-1),
                                  time_psiT = rep(0, my.constants$T-1),
                                  time_psiF = rep(0, my.constants$T-1),
                                  z = zinit)

_____________________________________________________________________________

My question is probably very basic but I could really use some help to avoid making any mistake!


I hope I've explained myself correctly!


Thank you so much!!
Iraida

parts:
Hi Iraida,

You're right, you don't have to provide initial values for those. Nimble would do that. But it does spit out that warning. You can provide initial values for those as long as they don't contract the model, but it shouldn't have much of an effect on your posteriors.

Regards,

Matt

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: Naive question about random year effects and initial values (Multivent model)
parts:
We generally recommend providing initial values for any top-level parameters (i.e., hyperparameters such as lambda.sigma2T) as drawing them from their prior (as nimble would do if they are not specified) can often produce unrealistic initial values. It's less critical in some cases, though still useful in many cases, to provide initial values for other parameters (i.e., other quantities specified stochastically via a distribution, such as time_psiT). And it's generally unnecessary to give initial values for anything specified deterministically (via assignment rather than specifying using a distribution, such as phi_maleT) as nimble will just run those calculations.

-chris
